column1: # Copyright (c) 2026 Contributors to the Eclipse Foundation.
# Who may reach what through the tag facade (#282) — the checklist that
# check-access.sh runs against a gateway and a broker, one row per case.
#   id      group/name; the group becomes the JUnit classname
#   caller  none | header:<raw Authorization value> | forged:<group> | client:<Keycloak client>
#   target  G:<path> through the gateway, B:<path> straight at the broker;
#           paths are taken as they are (no normalisation)
#   expect  a status (403), a class (4xx), or not one (!200)
#   check   optional, on the body: refs=<n> | has:<text> | lacks:<text>
#   why     what the row stands for
# The tags the Payment example seeds: payment/method/{paypal,card},
# the group /tags/payment/terms/instant, shop-credit the same with
# /tags/payment/terms/installment, shop-norole the instant group and no role.

column7: why

an empty bearer header is no token
a token that cannot be decoded names no group
basic credentials are not a token
a forged token passes the policy, which only decodes, and is refused by the facade, which verifies

the group passes the gateway, the missing tags-consumer stops it at the facade
an administrator passes the policy but holds no tags-consumer for the facade

card serves both contracts; under instant its answer names only Payment
